text: It seems like it would be useful to have more red teaming services for individuals. E.g. you can agree to have your credit  card company occasionally try common financial scams on you and tell you the results, so that you're more vigilant and aware of potential vulnerabilities.

author: AmandaAskell
text: I have much more confidence in media sources if they adhere to basic norms like "cite and link to primary sources and not just to other news outlets". I was reading stories about an Oxfam report from Time, The Guardian, and CNN. Not one of them linked to the report in question.

text: Seeing complex strategies and cooperative behaviors emerge without explicit training is really interesting. In this case, it's also adorable.

author: AmandaAskell
text: I think that AI is more likely to be broadly beneficial if the AI community takes a cooperative approach to its safety, security, and social impact. Excited to hear from others interested in this work, or in developing and implementing cooperative strategies.

quoted.text: Our newest policy research analyzes the game theory of industry cooperation on AI safety. We found 4 strategies the AI community can use today to enable long-term cooperation: https://t.co/AxMBQwORec https://t.co/VO8NDVeJKJ

author: AmandaAskell
text: @fchollet @Miles_Brundage One difficulty is that the point at which you should switch to a partial release is likely to be a point of incremental improvement (if progress is fairly continuous) but it's hard to make that switch without implying that your model is different in kind from what's come before.

author: AmandaAskell
text: I recommend this thread by Josh and think question (3) of where to draw the line is very difficult. The fact that you can delay the release of something but can't un-release it is one reason to err on the conservative side when industry-wide norms haven't been established.

quoted.text: I'd like to weigh in on the #GPT2 discussion. The decision not to release the trained model was carefully considered and important for norm-forming. Serving the public good requires us to draw lines on release somewhere: better long before catastrophe than after.
